You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtilsTest.testParseOctal() probes that TarUtils.parseOctal accepts:
  - pure octal digits ("777777777777"),
  - the same value with a trailing space,
  - with a trailing NUL,
  - and also fields that are entirely NULs or spaces: {0,0}, {0,' '}, {' ',0}.
- The last three inputs simulate how TAR headers may encode empty/zero values (UID/GID/size) using NULs/spaces.

What the code does:
- TarUtils.parseOctal(byte[], int, int):
  - If the first byte is NUL, it immediately returns 0 (lines 111–113), so {0,0} and {0,' '} work.
  - It skips leading spaces (lines 115–122).
  - It trims trailing NULs and spaces (lines 124–132).
  - If nothing remains after trimming, it throws IllegalArgumentException (lines 133–136).
  - Otherwise, it parses remaining digits, ensuring each byte is between '0' and '7' (lines 138–147).

Where it fails:
- For buffer {' ', 0}:
  - First byte is not NUL, so it doesn’t take the early-return path.
  - Leading spaces are skipped, start becomes 1.
  - Trailing NUL is trimmed, end becomes 1.
  - Now start == end, so the method throws IllegalArgumentException at lines 133–136.
- The test expects such an “all whitespace/NUL” field to be treated as zero, not as an error.

Relation to the issue report:
- The report “Incorrect handling of NUL username and group Tar.gz entries” describes failures parsing headers when certain fields are empty/NUL. Tar headers often use blank/NUL-padded fields for numeric values (e.g., uid/gid). With the current logic, fields that are entirely spaces and/or NULs but don’t start with NUL will hit the start==end case and throw.
- This stricter behavior was not present in 1.7 (which effectively treated empty/blank numeric fields as zero). In 1.8, the added “throw if empty after trimming” path causes IOException “Error detected parsing the header” to bubble up from TarArchiveInputStream when parseOctal throws.

Root cause:
- TarUtils.parseOctal incorrectly rejects fields that consist solely of spaces and/or NULs unless the very first byte is NUL. After trimming, an empty field should be treated as zero rather than an error.

Impact:
- Archives with numeric header fields encoded as blank/space/NUL (common for “unset” uid/gid/size in some tools) cause header parse failures.
- The unit test reproduces this via the {' ', 0} case.
